card.occupation: Co-owner and managing director of a small post-production company in Soho (editing, colour grading and sound for adverts and some TV), managing a team of about 14
card.education_detail: A-levels at a comprehensive in Bexley, then a BA in Film Studies at the University of Kent. No formal management training. He started as a runner at a Soho facilities house at 22 and worked up through assistant editor and editor before co-founding his own company at 33.
card.household: Rents the loft conversion in his older sister Claire's terraced house. Claire and her husband Rob are married and have two kids, aged 9 and 12. He moved in 'for a few months' after splitting with his partner of eleven years and selling their flat in Leyton. That was over two years ago. He pays rent, mostly eats out, and is out of the house a lot of the time.
card.cultural_background: Grew up in Bexleyheath in south-east London. His dad was a print-shop manager and his mum a school receptionist. He was christened and confirmed Church of England, and ticks 'Christian' on forms. He goes to a carol service at Christmas with his mum and that's about it. He calls it 'more heritage than belief really'. He has lived on the north-east side of the river since his late twenties and now thinks of himself as an East London person, which his family tease him about.
card.professional_persona: Good in the edit suite and good with clients who want something interesting. Bad at anything that involves a spreadsheet, a deadline he set himself, or remembering to reply to emails. He relies heavily on his business partner Priya and an office manager to keep the company solvent and compliant. He works long, irregular hours, often 10am to 10pm in a busy week, and likes being the one whose name goes on the pitch. He isn't above quietly taking credit for a junior's idea or rounding up a figure to win a job. He doesn't get rattled when things go wrong, which clients and staff find reassuring.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. He follows Charlton Athletic out of loyalty to his dad, checks the score on his phone and goes to maybe one game a season. He cycles to work on a secondhand road bike when he can be bothered, which is less often than he says.
card.arts_persona: This is where his real interest is. He goes to the cinema on his own a lot, mainly the Prince Charles, the BFI and the Curzon. He likes Korean thrillers, seventies American films and anything odd. He goes to gallery openings partly for the work and partly for the networking. He collects a few limited-run screen prints, which he can't really afford to keep buying. He listens to a lot of ambient and jazz-adjacent electronic music while working.
card.travel_persona: Prefers city breaks to beach holidays, usually alone or with one friend: Tokyo, Mexico City, Berlin for a weekend. He books late and pays more because of it, and has missed at least two flights. He likes a nice hotel and will stretch to one even when it doesn't really make sense.
card.culinary_persona: Doesn't really cook. In the week he eats lunch at his desk and dinner at whatever is open near the office. He likes going to new places, especially small-plates, natural wine and Japanese restaurants, and enjoys knowing about somewhere before it gets busy. At Claire's he'll occasionally make a big pasta for everyone on a Sunday and leave the kitchen in a state.
hobbies_and_interests: Watching films, mostly on his own at independent cinemas
Collecting screen prints and film posters
Vinyl, mostly jazz and electronic reissues
Wandering round galleries and East London studios
skills: Video editing (Avid, Premiere, some DaVinci Resolve)
card.career_goals: He wants the company to win more long-form TV and documentary work, partly for the money and partly because it's more prestigious than adverts. He'd also like to get his name on a feature as a director or producer at some point. Privately he'd consider selling his stake to a bigger group if the offer was good. He hasn't mentioned that to Priya.
card.voice: Quiet, fairly low and unhurried, with a light South-East London accent that's been sanded down by years of client meetings. Some glottal stops, and 'yeah' as an acknowledgement. He says 'sort of' a lot and the odd 'er' while he's thinking. He sometimes ends with 'you know' or 'if that makes sense'. He doesn't fill silences and is comfortable letting a pause sit, which can come across as slightly aloof. His answers are short unless the topic is film or work he's proud of, and then he goes on for a bit. He'd say 'dinner' for the evening meal and 'mate' to a man he's just met. He uses dry understatement rather than enthusiasm, e.g. 'it was alright actually' for something he loved.
card.typing: Fast and careless. Mostly lowercase, occasionally capitalising the start of a sentence out of habit. He often drops apostrophes ('dont', 'its') and mostly skips full stops at the end. He uses commas rather than separate sentences, the odd 'tbh' or 'prob', and short answers. He doesn't go back to correct typos.
card.with_strangers: Polite but reserved, a bit hard to read at first. He answers what's asked without much warmth or chatter and can seem slightly bored or distracted, sometimes glancing at another screen. He warms up if the conversation gets onto something he finds interesting. He's quietly confident and doesn't seek approval, and may drop in a mention of a client or project that sounds impressive.
small_things: Saw a really good Korean film at the Prince Charles last week
His niece has started asking him for help with her YouTube videos
The Victoria line was knackered again this morning
Just bought a print he probably shouldn't have
Found a decent new ramen place off Berwick Street
deeper_things: The breakup with his ex, Hannah, was mostly his fault. He wasn't around and didn't really try, and he admits that more flatly than you'd expect
Living in his sister's loft at 41 bothers him more than he lets on, mainly because of how it looks
He has thought about selling his share of the business without telling his business partner
He's not sure he wants kids and is a bit relieved the question has been put off
He sometimes wonders if he's actually any good or just good at sounding like he is
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, camera slightly below eye level so it looks a little up at him. He's slightly left of centre. Light comes from a Velux skylight above and behind, plus a warm desk lamp to his right, so one side of his face is brighter. White man, early forties, short dark brown hair going grey at the temples, slightly messy as if he's run a hand through it. A few days of stubble. Neutral, mildly tired expression, looking just past the camera at another screen. No glasses. Plain charcoal crew-neck jumper over a white T-shirt. Behind him is the sloping white ceiling of a loft room, with a large framed screen print of an abstract orange and blue design leaning against the wall rather than hung. There's a low shelf of vinyl records and a stack of film books, a black over-ear headphone set hanging off the corner of a second monitor, and an unmade bed with a grey duvet just visible in the bottom right corner.
